text:
oliver: quick share — our long-context runs (1M+ tokens) show steady KV-cache hole growth and RSS creeping up. heap/profile attached to the thread; flame graphs point at allocator churn in the small-block arena. anyone seen this pattern before?

maria: can you paste the eviction logs and the p50/p95 mem from the canary? curious if it's per-tenant or global.

oliver: eviction log snippet from canary-3 (last 2 hours):
`evict_attempts=12453 evictions_success=8272 holes_created=4921 compactions_triggered=18`
overall RSS delta +1.1GB over 3h on the 8k batch long-context test.

sam: that holes_created number jumps out. looks like allocator is leaving many small free ranges that never get reused. probably fragmentation + allocation pattern from long kv sequences.

jia: two high-level levers we discussed before: 1) tune block size or bucket sizing for the small-block allocator; 2) add compaction that relocates live entries into contiguous blocks. both have tradeoffs (copy cost, pauses).

maria: another axis is eviction prioritization. right now we evict by LRU-ish timestamp and tenant weight; if we instead bias eviction to prefer freeing ranges that reduce fragmentation (coalesce-friendly), we might avoid full compactions.

oliver: i ran a quick experiment: enable background compaction w/ 10% CPU budget. result: RSS down 18% after 1h, holes down ~70%. BUT p99 latency spiked +120ms during compaction bursts. definitely must be throttled carefully.

sam: can we make compaction incremental and relocation-bounded? e.g., move up to N bytes per cycle and only when tail-latency slack > threshold. also prefer relocating cold items.

jia: sketch of scoring for compaction vs eviction I threw together (pseudocode):
```
compaction_score = frag_ratio * idle_factor * (1 - recent_hit_rate) * age_boost
if compaction_score > threshold and cpu_budget>min -> schedule relocation(batch_limit)
```
frag_ratio = reclaimed_bytes_if_compacted / region_size

maria: +1 on the score. also add tenant_fairness multiplier so a noisy tenant can't monopolize compaction cycles. e.g. multiply by (1 / tenant_compaction_running_count).

sam: question about correctness: do we need a stop-the-world phase while we move entries? or can we use atomic pointer swapping + tombstones? moving live k/v safely is painful at high QPS.

jia: we can do lock-free relocation with generation tags: write new slot, update pointer atomically, leave old slot tombstoned and reclaimed by background reclamation. adds a bit of complexity but avoids global pauses.

perf-bot: auto-report: compaction-run@1849502380 freed=4.2MB moved_objects=12 cpu_pct=9 tail_latency_impact_ms=35

oliver: that's promising. the 35ms tail shows we still need tighter windows. my concern: long-context sequences keep creating small, short-lived KV entries (per-token cache slices) which bloat fragmentation. maybe we should special-case long-context workload: larger per-request allocation buckets to keep prefixes contiguous.

maria: yep — two-tier allocator idea: if estimated_seq_len > X, allocate from "long-context arena" with bigger chunk sizes (e.g., 64k) to avoid many small allocations. fallback for smaller sequences keeps current small-block behavior.

sam: tradeoff: bigger arenas increase internal waste for small seqs if misclassified. can mitigate by sampling and adaptive thresholds.

oliver: opened a draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4791 — "fragmentation: priority scheduler + long-context arena". includes feature flag and perf harness. requesting reviews from @maria, @jia.

maria: I'll review. please add unit tests that simulate heavy long-context churn and assert no regressions on p99. also add a perf regression guard in CI (run short long-context blast test).

jia: will sketch a regression test harness today. also propose a canary rollout plan: enable flag on 5% nodes, monitor holes_created and p99, then 20% if stable.

sam: i'll add telemetry: per-region frag_ratio gauge, compaction_cpu_pct, and per-tenant compaction_runs. set alerts if compaction_cpu_pct > 25% or frag_ratio > 0.3 for 30m.

oliver: thanks all. next steps: PR reviews, add tests + metrics, canary rollout. if we see worse tail we gate the flag. tagging followups: #4791, perf-harness ticket perf-117.

perf-bot: note: scheduled background compaction job disabled by default (feature flag off) — will only run in canary when flag=true.
